newsitem.title: FINLAND: Suunto says buys Swiss Recta AG.
newsitem.headline: Suunto says buys Swiss Recta AG.

text.p: Finnish compass maker Sunnto Oy said on Thursday it had acquired Swiss compass maker Recta AG for FIM 13 million, lifting its total output to over 1.5 million compasses -- a third of the global market.

It also said it had reached a long-term agreement with Johnson JWA, the second largest manufacturer of outdoor products in the U.S. and the largest seller of field compasses in North America, to deliver almost all compasses Johnson needs.

"As a result of these agreements, the net sales of Suunto's compass production will be almost doubled to more than FIM 70 million," it said, adding it would become the leading compass manufacturer in the world.

"The total number of compasses manufactured at Suunto's and Recta's factories will exceed 1.5 million compasses, which means that the market share of Suunto will exceed one third of the global market," Suunto said.
It saw scope for economies of scale.

"With the products of Suunto and Recta, Suunto will become market leader in the important North American and Central European markets, and can in the future make its production even more efficient thanks to the increasing volume," it said.
The acquisition and the agreement with Johnson would affect Suunto's result from the beginning of next year, Suunto said. @
Suunto said Recta's profitability had been good.
This year, Suunto's result before taxes would remain good, "even though it is likely to be somewhat lower than the result of the previous year," Suunto said.
Suunto had earlier estimated its net result this year to be lower that last year due to higher taxes.
In 1995, Suunto's pretax profit jumped to 30.1 million markka from 9.2 million and its profit after taxes but before appropriations was 25.7 million markka.
